messages:
devon: quick retro from this morning's cache-surge incident — want a compact owners checklist so followups don't slip. main signals: sudden KV residency bump, 95th latency spike, OOM on a subset of hosts.
prateek: +1. can we keep this thread strictly action items + owners? saves followups.
anya: adding context — saw fragmentation pattern on heap snapshots after ~2h of heavy traffic, not gradual growth. might be slab hot-path interaction.
maria: I ran a quick pprof dump before the nodes were cycled: 
```bash
curl -sS http://host:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-2026-03-23.pb
```
found large resident blocks pinned to LRU due to small-slab churn.
devon: ok concrete checklist: (1) short-term guardrails, (2) profiling automation, (3) targeted GC/eviction tuning, (4) regression detection + runbook edits. propose owners below.
prateek: i can own (1) guardrails: set soft-residency-limit to 80% of current avg and add auto-restart annotation for hosts that hit 95% within 10m. ETA: Thu EOD.
anya: i'll take (2) profiling automation. plan: add nightly heap-snapshot job (three samples: low/med/high qps) + auto-upload to s3, with pointer in the postmortem. ETA: next Tue.
maria: happy to take (3) tuning: try increasing slab reclaim aggressiveness and experiment with a 50ms background compact once-per-hour. will run canary on 3 hosts and report latency/cost delta. ETA: next Wed canary start.
devon: i'll own (4) runbook/regression detection: add latency + residency composite alert, and a quick dashboard tile with a 7d heatmap. also add a recurring monthly review slot. ETA: Fri.
prateek: one blocker: we need a clear rollback plan if compacting spikes latency. maria, can you define rollback triggers?
maria: yes — rollback if 95th latency increases >15% for 10m OR error rate + timeout rate up >0.5%. will post exact Grafana query in docs.
ops-bot: deployment scheduled: canary-start-job by maria at 2026-03-25T09:00Z (automated).
sre-runbook-bot: NOTE: incident template updated to include 'cache-surge' checklist link — /runbooks/cache-surge-checklist.
anya: quick ask — for profiling automation, what retention do we want for snapshots? 90 days seems ok but storage cost might be high. opinions?
prateek: 60 days + sampled older monthly summary is fine.
devon: decision: 60d retention + monthly archive. i'll update ticket.
prateek: small actionable: post the heap diff snippet you used, maria. that helped triage.
maria: pasted in ticket #INC-4321 (link) with diff and top-5 allocation stacks.
anya: adding test plan item: run memory-stress harness with our prefix-cache workload for 2h during canary. i'll coordinate windows.
devon: final notes: owners and ETAs captured, i'll open a single parent followup ticket with sub-tasks and weekly reminders. please react with :white_check_mark: once you have calendar time blocked.
prateek: ✅
anya: ✅
maria: ✅
devon: thanks all — keeping this tight should prevent the same pattern next month.
